Contributing to bioToolkit

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Naming conventions

One naming scheme across the package. Every new function follows it; existing functions are renamed when their roadmap item is worked on.

Function names

Kind Scheme Examples
Plots of a Seurat object, per cell <SeuratName>_bioToolkit (drop-in replacements users recognise) DimPlot_bioToolkit, FeaturePlot_bioToolkit, DotPlot_bioToolkit, VlnPlot_bioToolkit, DoHeatmap_bioToolkit, DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit
Plots of tables / matrices (DE, enrichment, bulk) plot_<thing>() plot_volcano, plot_ma, plot_pca, plot_variance_explained, plot_fc_quadrant, plot_de_dots, plot_enrichment_dots, plot_enrichment_bars, plot_composition_scatter
Data helpers verb first standardize_de(), standardize_enrichment(), top_markers(), export_source_data()
Palettes bt_palette(); verb first for the rest bt_palette(), list_palettes(), show_palettes(), check_palette()
ggplot2 extensions ggplot2’s own scheme, with bioToolkit theme_bioToolkit()
Saving save_plot() replaces save_dimplot(); save_umap() removed

Argument names

Seurat-style dot.case everywhere, with one shared vocabulary: the same meaning has the same name and the same default in every function.

Argument Meaning
group.by, split.by group.by: the lower-level grouping whose levels are compared, marked by their colours (violins, dot-plot rows, heatmap columns); split.by: the higher-level grouping, drawn like facets (labelled blocks or panels). E.g. group.by = "condition", split.by = "cell_type" compares conditions within each cell type. (Seurat’s VlnPlot / DotPlot use split.by the other way round.)
cols discrete colours (named or ordered) or a palette name — never colors / palette
na.value colour of missing / non-coloured marks
pt.size, alpha point size and opacity
label, label.size, label.n text labels and how many to draw
legend.position, legend.text.size, legend.title legend
panel.width, panel.height (inches) fixed panel size
cell.width, cell.height (inches) fixed size of one row / column of a grid plot
raster, raster.dpi rasterize the marks only; raster.dpi defaults to 1000 everywhere
bg background
seed randomness, without touching the global RNG (with_seed())
logfc.col, p.col, padj.col, mean.col, feature.col columns of a DE table

Default resolution: every rasterized output (raster.dpi, the dpi of save_plot() and of functions that save figures) defaults to 1000 dpi.

There are no size presets: one set of sizes (theme_sizes(): 11 / 9 / 12 pt text, 1 pt axes, 0.5 pt other lines) applies everywhere. Text-size arguments (legend.text.size, strip.text.size, …) default to NULL, meaning “from theme_sizes()”, so that the text sizes are set in one place; other sizes have plain numeric defaults.

Code style

Function definitions list one parameter per line, never several on a line:

plot_volcano <- function(
    data,
    method = c("auto", "edgeR", "DESeq2", "limma", "seurat"),
    feature.col = NULL
) {

or, aligned with the parenthesis:

standardize_de <- function(data,
                           method = c("auto", "edgeR", "DESeq2", "limma", "seurat"),
                           feature.col = NULL) {

This applies to all package-level functions, exported or internal. Short anonymous functions inside code (function(x) ...) are exempt.

Code should be easy to read line by line (user decision, 2026-10-14):

  • ggplot / patchwork: one layer per line; never several + (or |, /) on one line.

    ggplot(df, aes(value, feature)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.6) +
    theme_bioToolkit()

  • Calls with several arguments that do not fit comfortably on one line (about 80 characters): one argument per line, the closing parenthesis on its own line. The same for long vectors (e.g. named colours), one element per line.

  • No deep nesting on one line: at most one level of {} or of a call inside a call’s arguments per line; give an inner value a name first (test <- glmQLFTest(...), then topTags(test)).

  • Comments go on their own line above the code, not after it.

This applies to the website guides (vignettes/articles/) and to all new or changed package code. The package code written before 2026-10-14 has not yet been reformatted to it; that is a separate, planned pass.

Every plot

Before a plotting item is marked done in dev/visualization_roadmap.md:

  • Follows the names above.
  • Fixed geometry: panel_size_theme() (continuous axes: panel.width, panel.height, with panel.height = panel.width as the default for scatter-type plots usually drawn square (volcano, PCA, embeddings, quadrant and composition scatter), so that panel.width alone resizes them; discrete axes: cell.width, cell.height with grid_panel_size() and grid_expansion()), and saves correctly with save_plot().
  • Uses theme_bioToolkit(). Colours: one cols argument with a good default, resolved by group_colours() for groups (palette name, or colours named by group or in level order) and resolve_continuous_palette() for continuous scales (palette name, or colours from low to high, e.g. c(low, mid, high)).
  • Gene names in italics (italic_labels(), feature_is_gene()).
  • Expression from Seurat objects: an assay argument (NULL = the default assay, as in Seurat) and slot; resolve them with resolve_assay(), which reports the assay and layer used, and fetch genes with fetch_features() (assay-keyed, so values never come from another assay). Write the assay and layer into the source data (R/seurat_data.R).
  • Grids of dots (genes x groups, terms x comparisons) use the dot-grid engine dot_grid_plot() (R/dot_grid.R) rather than drawing their own.
  • Legend extractable with extract_legend() (works for any ggplot; nothing to do unless the plot hides its legend in an unusual way).
  • Source data recoverable with export_source_data(): the tidy table in plot$data, or in attr(plot, "source_data") when layers use different data.
  • roxygen docs with an example; devtools::document() re-run.
  • Unit tests for the data logic in tests/testthat/.
  • Checked by eye on real data.
  • NEWS.md entry, including anything removed or renamed.
  • On the website: listed in a reference section of _pkgdown.yml (the pkgdown build fails otherwise) and shown, with each mode of its arguments, in the matching guide in vignettes/articles/ (see dev/documentation_site.md). The site is published when the version in DESCRIPTION changes.

Adding a colour palette

Add an entry to palette_list() in R/palettes.R with its source, copying hex values from the primary source (or a package reproducing it), never from memory. The tests in tests/testthat/test-palettes.R check every entry.
